Subject: Pricing appendix redlines (stability margin trigger)

Hi Hannah —

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. We attached our redlines to the pricing exhibit; the primary ask is clarity on the proposed 'stability margin' trigger and the interaction with minimum monthly fees. Key points for us:

- We need a clear definition of the metric that would cause reversion of discounts (is it peak monthly usage, 30-day rolling average, or another measure?).
- We want caps to be symmetrical (both upside and downside) and a defined notice period before any retro adjustments.
- Our procurement team is sensitive to retroactive true-ups that could materialize on renewal.

Attached: NovaHealth_Redline_20261108.docx (track changes) and a short diff (pricing-exhibit-diff-20261108.txt).

Can you confirm whether Redwood is open to: (a) tying the trigger to a 30-day rolling usage average, (b) limiting lookback true-up to 60 days, and (c) adding an annual cap on accumulated retroactive charges?

Appreciate a short summary and proposed language to share with our legal team before the next contracting call.

Best,
Marta Alvarez
Director, Procurement
NovaHealth

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-08T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Pricing appendix redlines (stability margin trigger)

Team — forwarding NovaHealth's redlines. They want a crisp definition and limits on retro true-ups. Quick asks below and attaching our internal analysis (hs-internal-analysis-20261108.pdf).

Priority items I'd like us to align on before I reply:
1) Metric definition: 30-day rolling average vs. calendar month peak — what can our billing system compute reliably?
2) Lookback window: Nova proposes 60 days; Legal prefers 90 for operational reconciliation. Can we compromise at 60?
3) Annual cap on retroactive charges — what's an acceptable percent of annual committed spend? Finance input needed.

Proposed next steps: Laura, can you draft two short alternatives (A and B) that I can send to Nova:
- A (customer-favorable): 30-day rolling average trigger, 60-day lookback, 10% annual cap on retro charges
- B (Redwood-favorable): calendar month peak trigger, 90-day lookback, no cap but monthly smoothing clause
Ben — feel free to propose a short canary/operational fallback we can offer to close faster (e.g., temporary grace for first quarter).

I want to keep this tight — Nova is asking for wording to show their legal team before Friday.

Thanks,
Hannah
Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-08T12:28:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pricing appendix redlines (stability margin trigger)

Hannah — draft language below. Kept clauses short so contracting can paste into the exhibit; added notes where operations/finance will need to implement changes.

ALTERNATIVE A (customer-favorable) — Suggested insertion into Exhibit B (Pricing):
"Stability Margin Trigger: The parties agree that a Stability Margin Trigger occurs when the Customer's 30-day rolling average of billable token units exceeds the Customer's committed monthly baseline by more than 120%. Upon occurrence of a Stability Margin Trigger, Redwood may, after providing thirty (30) days' written notice, adjust the unit pricing for subsequent invoices. Any true-up for the period that triggered the adjustment shall be limited to amounts invoiced within the prior sixty (60) calendar days, and retroactive charges shall not exceed ten percent (10%) of Customer's billed charges for the applicable twelve (12) month period."

Operational notes (for ops/finance):
- Billing must compute 30-day rolling avg daily; flag triggers and generate automated notices.
- True-up scope limited to 60-day lookback; need a reconciliation runbook.

ALTERNATIVE B (Redwood-favorable):
"Stability Margin Trigger: A Stability Margin Trigger occurs when Customer's peak calendar month billable token units exceed Customer's committed monthly baseline by more than 150%. Redwood may provide ninety (90) days' notice before adjusting unit pricing. Any reconciliations will be smoothed across the following three (3) invoices to mitigate billing shock."

I recommend we present both options and highlight operational impacts. If Finance can sign off on the 10% cap and Ops confirms we can compute the 30-day rolling avg reliably, I think Alternative A is a clean path to close.

—Laura
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
